Philips is one of the largest medical technology companies in the world, where patient safety depends on customers being properly trained before they use its equipment. That responsibility falls to a Global Education team navigating hundreds of process steps across systems that do not talk to each other, relying on workshops and best guesses to find inefficiencies. In three months, Mimica helped the team uncover 3,700 hours of automation potential, worth up to €700,000 a year.

_During a recent webinar, Mimica CEO Tuhin Chakraborty, Jan Lont, Director of Customer Support for Global Education at Philips, and Rob de Graaf, Senior Consultant in Innovation Management at Philips, discussed how Mimica helped uncover huge automation possibilities that could save thousands of hours a year. The case study below is based on their discussion. To watch the full video_ [_click here_](https://www.mimica.ai/webinars/how-philips-uncovered-3-700-hours-of-hidden-automation-potential-in-3-months) _._

At Philips, one of the largest medical technology companies in the world, patient safety drives every decision. When a customer buys from Philips, the sale doesn't end at delivery. They need training, onboarding, and support before they can use the technology safely and effectively, and that's where [Jan Lont's](https://www.linkedin.com/in/jan-lont-b575674/) team comes in. As Director of Customer Support for Global Education, Jan runs a department that sits at a critical junction in Philips' ability to deliver on its promises.

The team is experienced, knowledgeable, and deeply invested in getting things right. But they were navigating a process that wound through multiple disconnected systems, hundreds of steps, and years of accumulated workarounds. Work that could have been handled automatically was being handled manually. And nobody had a clean, complete picture of the full workflow or where opportunities for optimization existed.
That changed when Philips partnered with Mimica.
## The challenge: processes that outpaced the documentation

citations.title: How McKesson Overcomes Out-of-Date SOPs and Tribal Knowledge with Mimica | Mimica
excerpts: # How McKesson Overcomes Out-of-Date SOPs and Tribal Knowledge with Mimica

‍McKesson is a Fortune 10 healthcare services company managing $400 billion in annual payables across a shared services organization of 1,400 people. At that scale, understanding how work actually gets done is not a simple problem. It turns out, most of the answers were locked inside people's heads.

_At SSOW 2026, Mimica CEO Tuhin Chakraborty sat down with Brandy Hulsey, VP of Enterprise AP & Reverse Logistics at McKesson, to discuss how process intelligence is powering one of the largest financial services transformations in healthcare. The case study below is based on their discussion._ [_To watch the full video click here._](https://www.mimica.ai/webinars/inside-mckessons-shared-services-transformation-how-process-intelligence-is-improving-accounts-payable-and-beyond)
## Institutional knowledge doesn’t tell the whole story
1,400 people doing back-office finance work can produce hundreds, if not thousands, of different workflows. Some of those variations are intentional. Most are not.

McKesson's shared services organization had a challenge familiar to any large enterprise: process knowledge had become muscle memory. Experienced employees could execute complex workflows quickly and reliably, but ask them to explain exactly how they did it and they struggled to pinpoint the step-by-step process.

"We have a lot of people that can do really great things," said [Brandy Hulsey, VP of Enterprise AP & Reverse Logistics](https://www.linkedin.com/in/brandy-hulsey-59b4b890/) , "but they can't tell you _how_ they do it, because they just do it second nature."

The documentation that did exist was often a 30-page SOP last updated years ago. When McKesson began its transformation initiative, AIM 28, a multi-year program targeting significant cost savings and efficiency gains across the enterprise, it became clear that they could not transform what they didn’t fully understand.
To get a clear picture of _all_ the ways work was being done, without any missing process steps or relying on out-of-date references, McKesson chose Mimica.
## Mimica identifies gap in internal tool adoption and hidden process inefficiencies
The clearest example of Mimica's impact at McKesson so far came from a tool McKesson had already built.

citations.title: Forward Deployed Engineer, Intelligent Automation @ Mimica
excerpts: [Mimica](https://www.mimica.ai/careers) is an AI-powered process intelligence platform enabling enterprises and individuals to reclaim their most precious resource: time. We've all seen repetitive tasks and redundant processes quietly drain productivity and creativity. Not because companies don’t want to become more efficient, but because they don’t know where to start.

Mimica automatically analyzes your team’s work, then generates the AI agents to execute it. Our software turns everyday work into data-backed decisions, helping companies remove process bottlenecks, automate the right tasks, and upskill teams with precision and confidence.

We’ve raised $26 million in Series B financing and are scaling fast. Backed by investors including Khosla Ventures and Paladin Capital, our proprietary AI technology is trusted by Fortune 500 companies to accelerate transformation. Mimica is recognized as a Top 100 AI Start-up by Accel and an industry Leader by the Everest Group.

Behind our platform is a team of exceptionally talented people, remote-first and globally distributed across 16+ countries. We're looking for curious, collaborative people excited to solve complex problems. You'll join a fast-paced environment built on high ownership, bottom-up thinking, and transparent, open communication – helping some of the world's leading organizations transform the way work gets done with AI.

We're hiring a Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) to join Mimica's Intelligent Automation team. You'll embed with our enterprise customers, turn process and task-mining insights into working automations, and get them into production fast. This is a hands-on, customer-facing engineering role with a strong focus on agentic AI.

You'll design and ship AI agents built on frontier models such as Claude and Gemini, combine them with RPA and custom code running on Google Cloud, and bring what you learn in the field back to our product and delivery playbooks. As a senior member of the team, you'll also act as a technical leader and mentor for our Intelligent Automation developers, helping them grow their skills in RPA, AI, and engineering best practices.
* Own customer deployments end to end – from discovery and solution design through build, testing, go-live and hypercare.
* Turn process insights into automations – use process and task-mining data to find, size and prioritize the highest-value opportunities.
* Design and build agentic AI solutions – create AI agents that reason, call tools and act across enterprise systems, using models such as Claude (Anthropic), Gemini (Google) and GPT (OpenAI).
* Pick the right model and pattern for the job – compare models on accuracy, cost, latency, and data-privacy needs, and choose between agents, LLM steps, RPA, or plain code.
* Make AI reliable in production – build evaluation sets, guardrails, human-in-the-loop checkpoints and monitoring so agents behave predictably at enterprise scale.

basis.reasoning: The Mimica job description explicitly names Claude (Anthropic), Gemini (Google), and GPT (OpenAI) as examples of models used to build its AI agents.
